findings.heading: ### F-02 (MAJOR, blocking) AC-1.1 contradicts the `/sc:load` row (zero/empty attack)
findings.body:
- Expert: Adzic (lead), Wiegers, Crispin-style completeness.
- Where: spec:203 (AC-1.1: "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`"), spec:112 (load: report "none (see note)", resume "n/a", "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task"), spec:159 (P1 includes load for "usage line only"), spec:62 (WC-4 requires a contract on every outcome), spec:274 (Decision: no report file for load, "a report file would be an unrequested addition").
- Grading check: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a load edit that adds only a usage-line fix and no contract (spec:112, spec:274), and AC-1.1 then fails, because it requires a section naming `return-contract.yaml` in every 3.1-3.2 command; or builds a contract for load, which spec:274 forbids. Both stated texts cannot hold, and the acceptance criterion cannot pass under the row as written.
- Recommendation: narrow AC-1.1 to name load as the exception (or exclude it from the loop), so no new text is needed for load.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Testability, about +1.

findings.heading: ### F-2 (blocking). AC-1.2 cannot pass for every command the P1 row names
findings.body:
- Severity: MAJOR, graded blocking because the acceptance criterion cannot pass on the stated text. Priority: High. Expert: Wiegers, Adzic. Quality-impact estimate: Testability drops about 2 points.
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text builds Phase 1 exactly as the P1 row says, and AC-1.2 then fails on four of the thirteen named commands.
- Evidence:
  - P1 row names load, workflow, index-repo and cleanup-audit among its commands (SPEC:159).
  - AC-1.2: "7.2 live check on each P1 command with `--unattended --output <dir>`" and "all steps pass" (SPEC:196). 7.2 step 3 requires the report path to be "the WC-4 contract path" and step 4 requires a contract file with a valid `status` (SPEC:182-183).
  - load: the P1 row gives "usage line only" and "none (see note)" for the report, with no `--unattended` and no contract (SPEC:112, 159). AC-1.1 correctly says "load excepted" (SPEC:195); AC-1.2 does not.
  - workflow: the contract path is inside a generated package directory and `--output` does not apply; the spec calls this a WC-4 exception (SPEC:62, 92, 182). `--output <dir>` is not a workflow flag in the spec.
  - index-repo: brief passes "none"; output is `PROJECT_INDEX.md` at an implied location (SPEC:86; INV-A:53).
  - cleanup-audit: output dir is fixed, `--pass <N>` (SPEC:85; INV-A:42).
- Recommendation (narrow): restate AC-1.2 as "each P1 command that gains `--unattended`, using the flags its section 3 row lists", and exempt load by name. Do not add flags to commands to make the criterion pass.
- Reviser may touch: SPEC:196 only.

findings.heading: ### F-01 (blocking, MAJOR) — AC-1.1 requires P1 to deliver work the spec assigns to P3/P4 and to undecided D2-D4
findings.body:
- Experts: Wiegers (traceability), Adzic (example), Crispin (acceptance).
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, in Phase 1, a `## Unattended mode` section in every command of sections 3.1-3.2 except `load` (including implement, post-release, pr-submit, roadmap, save, validate-roadmap, validate-tests), because AC-1.1 asserts exactly that (S:195) and "Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks in section 7 pass" (S:154); and that is wrong because the same spec says the P1 command list is nine commands plus three fixes (S:159), the gate resolutions of those other commands are defined by phases P2-P4 (S:160-162), "Phases 1-3 need no user decision; Phase 4 waits for answers to D2-D4" (S:154, S:225), and under the recommended D3(a) "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (S:240). So P1 either fails AC-1.1 (the P4 commands and the 3.1 commands not in the S:159 list lack the section) or ships implement/post-release/pr-submit gate text before D2-D4 are answered. Section 2.1 makes this worse: each section "lists only its own gate resolutions" (S:52), so a P1 section for `implement` must already contain the D2 outcome.
- Also in conflict: S:159 says the flag is "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 except `load`" while its Commands column lists only analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test, load plus three fixes; S:128 says section-4 commands get no mode, but D3(a) leaves pr-submit with none either (S:139, S:240), so AC-1.1 cannot assert both.
- Recommendation (narrowing, no new rule): scope AC-1.1 and the S:159 flag sentence to the commands listed in the P1 row; let each later phase's own check (AC-2.1, AC-3.x, AC-4.x) cover the `## Unattended mode` section of the commands it converts; state that pr-submit has no section unless D3(b) is chosen.
- Priority High. Quality impact: removes a phase-gate that no implementer can pass as written.

findings.heading: ### F-1. BLOCKING, MAJOR. P1 scope, the phase column and AC-1.1 contradict each other (Wiegers, Whittaker). Priority High.
findings.body:
- Sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a P1 in which `--unattended` and a `## Unattended mode` section exist on commands whose gates are converted only in P2/P3/P4. That is wrong because WC-2 and WC-9 say `--unattended` never prompts and never takes an outward default. Alternatively the implementer builds only the P1 command list, and AC-1.1 then fails.
- Text A: P1 scope says "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 except load (B-2) (a no-op where a command has no gate)" (spec:159).
- Text B: AC-1.1 requires the section on "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 except load" (spec:195).
- Text C: the Commands column of P1 lists only nine no-gate commands plus fixes to four ready ones (spec:159).
- Text D: the Phase column assigns auggie-review, cleanup, improve, cli-eval, cli-portify, recommend, research, review-translation, spec-panel, task and tasklist to P2 (spec:100-122), roadmap, save, validate-roadmap and validate-tests to P3, and implement, post-release and pr-submit to P4.
- Counted evidence: brainstorm and init-lite (3.1, "Small fix: None", spec:84,87) appear in no phase's Commands column at all. Yet 3.1 says "The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column" (spec:79) while AC-1.1 requires both to gain the section.
- Wrong outcome: auggie-review in P1 would accept `--unattended` and still post a review to GitHub and end its turn on a chat offer (`INV-A:62`, `INV-A:76`).
- Wrong outcome: AC-1.2 checks only "each P1 command", so nothing catches this.
- Recommendation: state per command which phase adds the flag and the section. A command whose gates are not yet converted must refuse `--unattended` until its phase lands. Narrow AC-1.1 to the commands of that phase.

findings.heading: ### F-01 (CRITICAL, blocking) P1 and AC-1.1 contradict D3 (a), section 4 and the "P4 waits for D2-D4" rule (expert: Wiegers, Nygard)
findings.body:
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written adds an `## Unattended mode` section and a `--unattended` flag to `/sc:pr-submit`, `/sc:post-release` and `/sc:implement` in Phase 1, and that is wrong because the same document says those three change only in Phase 4 after the user answers D2-D4, and recommends that pr-submit get no change at all.
- Texts in conflict:
  - S:159: Phase 1 scope is "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2", and S:195 (AC-1.1) requires every command in 3.1-3.2 except `/sc:load` to have the section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`. Sections 3.1-3.2 include implement (S:109), post-release (S:113) and pr-submit (S:114), each tagged phase P4.
  - S:154: "Phases 1-3 need no user decision; Phase 4 waits for answers to D2-D4."
  - S:240 (D3 (a), recommended): "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4". S:128 and S:139: coordinator-only commands "get no `--unattended` mode"; pr-submit "stays a worker candidate only if the user accepts" D3.
  - S:52: the section is added by "each changed command".
- Concrete trace: D3 answered (a) (the recommendation, on which S:225 says Phases 0-3 proceed). P1 ships. AC-1.1 passes only if pr-submit has the section, so pr-submit has been edited; D3 (a) says it is not edited. Both cannot hold. The same applies to implement (D2) and post-release (D4).
- Recommendation: restrict P1 scope and AC-1.1 to the commands whose section-3 phase is P1-P3, and exempt the three P4 commands (and pr-submit under D3 (a)) by name, as S:195 already does for `/sc:load`.
- Priority: High.

findings.heading: ### F-2 (blocking) AC-1.1 cannot pass for `/sc:load`
findings.body:
- Severity: MAJOR, graded blocking. Experts: Wiegers (traceability), Adzic (testable example).
- Location: S:195 (AC-1.1) against S:112 (load row), S:265 (Decisions: load handling), S:52 and S:76 (every changed command gains the section), S:62 (WC-4).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written adds a `## Unattended mode` section to `/sc:load` (it is "changed": its usage line, S:112) and AC-1.1 requires every command in 3.1-3.2 to have such a section "naming `return-contract.yaml`"; that is wrong because the load row says Report "none" and "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task" (S:112) and the Decisions table says a report file "would be an unrequested addition" (S:265), so the test either fails for load or forces the contract the spec rejects. Two stated texts contradict (AC-1.1 against S:112 and S:265).
- Recommendation: exempt `load` from AC-1.1 and from WC-4 in one line (the narrower edit); do not add a contract to load.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Testability 7 -> 5.

findings.heading: ### F-01 (CRITICAL by label, blocking) `/sc:load` is required to have a contract and is required not to (Wiegers, Adzic)
findings.body:
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a P1 `test_worker_contract.py` and a `/sc:load` that satisfy AC-1.1 and AC-1.2, and X is wrong because the same document says `/sc:load` has no report file and must not get one, so one stated text or the other fails.
- Stated texts:
  - spec:76 "Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section"; spec:79 / spec:62 (WC-4) contract "written on every outcome".
  - spec:112 `load`: report "none (see note)", resume "n/a", change "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task", phase "P1 (usage line only)"; spec:265 (Decisions): "a report file would be an unrequested addition".
  - spec:159 lists `load (usage line only)` in the P1 scope.
  - spec:195 AC-1.1: the test asserts that "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`". `load` is in 3.2 (spec:112).
  - spec:196 AC-1.2: a 7.2 live check "on each P1 command with `--unattended --output <dir>`"; 7.2 step 4 (spec:183) requires `test -s <contract>` with `status` and `command`. `load` is a P1 command (spec:159) and has no contract.
- Concrete trace: P1 test run -> `load.md` has no `## Unattended mode` section, as spec:112 asks -> AC-1.1 fails. Adding the section with a contract creates the "unrequested" report that spec:265 forbids. The same holds for AC-1.2 step 4.
- Recommendation: state `load` as an explicit exception in AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 (and in spec:76), or give it a contract and delete the spec:112 / spec:265 position. Pick one.
- Priority High. Quality impact: Testability / Consistency.

findings.heading: ### B-1 (CRITICAL, blocking) AC-1.2 requires a contract and `--output <dir>` from P1 commands that the spec says have neither
findings.body:
- Location: `SPEC:206` (AC-1.2), against `SPEC:159`, `SPEC:62` (WC-4), `SPEC:86`, `SPEC:85`, `SPEC:112`, `SPEC:167`.
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a P1 live check that runs "each P1 command with `--unattended --output <dir>`" and requires `all steps pass`, including 7.2 step 4 `test -s <contract>` (`SPEC:193`); and builds a phase gate that says "A phase passes only when every check in its block ... passes" (`SPEC:167`). The P1 row (`SPEC:159`) lists `load` ("usage line only, no section"), whose row says "Report: none" and "use it as a step inside another worker's brief" (`SPEC:112`) and which AC-1.1 itself excludes (`SPEC:205`); it also lists `index-repo` ("Brief must pass: none", report `PROJECT_INDEX.md`, `SPEC:86`) and `cleanup-audit` (`--pass <N>`, `SPEC:85`), which WC-4 names as having no output flag (`SPEC:62`). Those commands accept neither `--unattended` nor `--output <dir>` and write no contract, so AC-1.2 cannot pass, P1 never passes, and "Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks ... pass" (`SPEC:154`) blocks P2-P4. The statement is wrong because AC-1.1 and 3.2 already carve `load` out and WC-4 already says which commands have no output flag; AC-1.2 does not.
- Expert: Wiegers (testability), Adzic (the example in the check contradicts the per-command rows).
- Recommendation: narrow AC-1.2 to "each P1 command that has a contract row" and name the exceptions (`load`; for `index-repo`, `cleanup-audit`, `workflow` the brief flags are those of their 3.1 rows, not `--output <dir>`). Delete rather than add: one clause.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: completeness and testability each about -1 until fixed.

=== ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS ===

No architecture finding reaches blocking. The decision itself (Orca on top, commands as units; `SPEC:16`, `SPEC:29-37`) is consistent with the evidence in the capabilities inventory (`CAPS:97-101`, `CAPS:147-150`, `CAPS:155-161`), and the spec states its own evidence gaps plainly (`SPEC:41-45`, `SPEC:282`).

findings.heading: ### F1 - CRITICAL-equivalent BLOCKING (MAJOR label): P1 acceptance check and P1 scope contradict the phase table and the user-decision gate
findings.body:
- Experts: Wiegers (traceability), Cockburn (who owns what), Whittaker (Sequence Attack).
- Priority: High.
- Stated texts that contradict (spec lines):
  - Line 159 (P1 scope): "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 except load".
  - Line 200 (AC-1.1, pass condition of P1): the test asserts "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 except load has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`".
  - Lines 109, 113, 114 (section 3.2 rows) and line 162 (P4): implement, post-release and pr-submit belong to P4. Line 154 says "Phases 1-3 need no user decision; Phase 4 waits for answers to D2-D4". Line 245 (D3 option a, the recommendation): "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4". Lines 124-125 and 118-119 place validate-roadmap, validate-tests, roadmap and save in P3. Line 162 says the coordinator "cannot predict their report path until they are fixed".
- Sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written adds a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` to pr-submit, implement, post-release, validate-roadmap, validate-tests and roadmap in Phase 1 so that AC-1.1 passes, and X is wrong because those sections need the gate resolutions that D2, D3 and D4 have not yet decided (and under the recommended D3(a) pr-submit is never changed), and for the P3 commands the report path the section would name is not defined until P3 reconciles command and skill (lines 118, 124).
- Whittaker, Sequence Attack: I can break this specification by **Sequence Attack**. The invariant at **section 6 / section 7.3 AC-1.1** (a phase leaves "later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks pass", line 154) fails when **P1's check demands artifacts that the phase table assigns to P2-P4**. Concrete attack: before = 3 commands (implement, post-release, pr-submit) with no section and an undecided D2-D4; step 1 an implementer runs AC-1.1; step 2 the test fails for those 3 (and for roadmap, save, validate-roadmap, validate-tests); step 3 the implementer either invents gate text for them (pre-empting D2-D4) or weakens the test; after = P1 cannot pass without a user decision, which line 154 says it does not need.
- Recommendation (delete or narrow, do not add): restrict AC-1.1 and the P1 flag/section scope to the commands the section 3 table gives P1 (analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test, plus the section 3.1 commands whose P1 fix is listed), or state per phase which commands the test covers.

findings.heading: ### B-1 (CRITICAL, blocking) AC-1.1 and the P1 scope contradict the phase column, D3(a), section 4 and the `load` row
findings.body:
Experts: Wiegers (traceability), Adzic.
Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a Phase 1 that adds a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` to all 37 worker-capable commands, and that is wrong because the same text says the opposite for several of them.
- `spec:195` (AC-1.1): the test "asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`". `spec:159` (P1 scope): "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2". Those sets contain 37 commands, including implement, post-release and pr-submit (P4).
- `spec:162` and `spec:154`: Phase 4 "waits for answers to D2-D4" and only applies them then; `spec:114` and `spec:239-242`: D3(a) (recommended, and `spec:225` says phases 0-3 proceed on the recommendations) is "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4", and `spec:139` says pr-submit stays a worker candidate only if D3 is accepted. Under D3(a) pr-submit is coordinator-only like the section-4 commands, but AC-1.1 requires it to carry a worker section at P1 (while `spec:195` also requires that no section-4 command has one).
- `spec:112`: the `load` row says Report "none (see note)" and Phase "P1 (usage line only)", and `spec:265` decides no report file for `load`; `spec:76` says only changed commands gain the section. AC-1.1 still demands that its section name `return-contract.yaml`, which `load` never writes.
- `spec:83-92`: brainstorm and init-lite have "Small fix: None" yet AC-1.1 requires a new section on them in P1.
Count trace (Quantity Flow): AC-1.1 asserts 37 sections at P1; the Phase column assigns 9 (3.2) + 3 or 4 (3.1 fixes: adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo, workflow) = 12-13 commands to P1 and 24 elsewhere; 3 of the 24 are P4 commands the spec says must wait for a user decision. AC-1.1 cannot be passed at the end of P1 without either breaking D3(a)/the P4 wait or failing on `load`.
Recommendation: restrict AC-1.1 and the P1 scope sentence to the commands whose Phase column is P1 (plus the 3.1 commands P1 touches), and let later phases add their own assertion (AC-2.1, AC-3.x, AC-4.x already do this); delete the `load` requirement to name `return-contract.yaml`. Priority High.

findings.heading: ### B-2 (MAJOR, blocking, High): AC-1.1 and the P1 scope contradict the `load` row
findings.body:
Experts: Wiegers, Adzic.
Texts that conflict:
- AC-1.1 asserts that "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`" (spec:195). P1 says the `--unattended` flag is "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)" (spec:159). The section 3 intro says "Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section" (spec:76).
- The `load` row says report "none (see note)", resume "n/a", and "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task"; its P1 scope is "usage line only" (spec:112, 159; Decisions row spec:265, `INV-B:31,65`).
Wrong outcome: an implementer who follows the `load` row edits only the Usage line, and AC-1.1 then fails because `load.md` has no Unattended section naming `return-contract.yaml`. An implementer who follows AC-1.1 adds a contract-naming section to a command the spec says writes no contract, which also breaks the SA-4 additive-only limit (spec:149) and the Decisions row "a report file would be an unrequested addition" (spec:265). Both cannot hold, and the acceptance criterion cannot pass under the row as written.
Recommendation (Wiegers): exclude `load` from AC-1.1 and from the P1 flag list by name, or give it a one-line Unattended section that says it writes no contract.
Quality impact: Consistency +1, Testability +1.

findings.heading: ### F-01 | MAJOR | BLOCKING | priority High | Wiegers, Adzic
findings.body:
**Issue.** The P1 acceptance test AC-1.1 cannot pass against the P1 scope the spec itself states.
- AC-1.1 (SPEC:195) asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, and (SPEC:171, SPEC:167) a phase passes only when every check in its block passes.
- `/sc:load` is a 3.2 command (SPEC:112) whose report is "none (see note)", whose resume is "n/a", and which "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task"; the P1 row lists it as "load (usage line only)" (SPEC:159) and the Decisions table says a report file "would be an unrequested addition" (SPEC:265). A section that names `return-contract.yaml` for load contradicts all three.
- AC-1.1 also covers the P4 commands `/sc:implement`, `/sc:post-release` and `/sc:pr-submit` (SPEC:109, 113, 114). Phase 4 "waits for answers to D2-D4" (SPEC:154), and D3's recommended option (a) says "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (SPEC:240). P1's scope sentence "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" (SPEC:159) reads the other way, while its Commands column lists only 9 commands plus 4 fixes.

**Grading sentence.** An implementer who follows the stated text as written (P1 Commands column and the load row) builds P1 with `/sc:load` untouched except for its usage line and with no `## Unattended mode` section on the P2-P4 commands, and that is wrong because AC-1.1, a P1 pass condition, then fails; the implementer who instead satisfies AC-1.1 must edit load, implement, post-release and pr-submit in P1, which SPEC:109-114, SPEC:154 and SPEC:240 forbid. Two stated texts contradict each other with no assumption needed.

**Recommendation.** Narrow AC-1.1's quantifier to the commands the section 6 P1 row names (plus the 3.1 commands whose section 3.1 row says P1), and let AC-2.1, AC-3.x and AC-4.x carry the same assertion for their own commands; say explicitly that `/sc:load` gets no `## Unattended mode` section. Rationale: deleting a clause is smaller than adding rules. Quality impact: removes an unpassable gate (testability +).

=== ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS ===

(No blocking architecture finding. The central decision, section 1, is supported: R1-R5 (SPEC:31-37) resolve to `CAPS:97-103`, `CAPS:145-150`; E4/E5 hold against `CAPS:155`. The spec states its evidence gaps itself (SPEC:41-45).)

findings.heading: #### F-02 MAJOR (blocking). Acceptance check AC-1.1 cannot pass at Phase 1, and under decision D3 option (a) can never pass
findings.body:
Expert: Adzic (testability), Wiegers.
Texts that contradict:
- AC-1.1 (SPEC:195): the test asserts that "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 whose row adds a section (not `load`, and not a 3.1 row whose small-fix column is `None`)" has a `## Unattended mode` section.
- Section 6 (SPEC:154) and 7 (SPEC:167): "Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks ... pass"; "A phase passes only when every check in its block ... passes."
- The rows themselves assign most of those commands to P2, P3 and P4 (SPEC:99-125, e.g. tasklist P2, roadmap P3, implement P4), and D3 option (a), the recommendation, says "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (SPEC:240).

Grading sentence: An implementer who builds the P1 test exactly as AC-1.1 is written asserts a section in about 34 commands, and that is wrong because 26 or more of those commands are not edited until P2-P4, so P1 cannot pass, P2 cannot start, and pr-submit (and any command declined under D2-D4) never gets the section the test demands.

Dimensional trace (Fowler, Pipeline Dimensional Analysis): see the Quantity Flow Diagram below. 37 dispatchable commands feed a test over 34, and P1 edits 13 (9 new plus 4 fixes, SPEC:159), so the "every command" assertion has no phase-scoped form in the text.
Quality impact: High (a gate that blocks the whole rollout).

findings.heading: ### F1 (CRITICAL, blocking): the P1 acceptance test and P1 scope contradict the spec's own per-row decisions
findings.body:
Experts: Wiegers (testability), Crispin (acceptance criteria), Fowler (phase boundaries).

An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a P1 that adds a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` to every command in sections 3.1-3.2, and X is wrong because three stated texts cannot all hold:

1. **`/sc:load` has no contract.** AC-1.1 (S:195) requires every command in sections 3.1-3.2 to have a `## Unattended mode` section "naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`". `/sc:load` is a section 3.2 row (S:112). The same document says "load has no contract, because it is not dispatched as its own Task" (S:76), the row says "Report: none (see note)" (S:112), and the Decisions table rejects a report file for load as "an unrequested addition" (S:265). AC-1.1 cannot pass without giving load a section that names a file load never writes, or adding the file the spec rejected. S:76 also says "Every changed command also gains the section", and load is changed (usage line, S:112), which makes S:112 and AC-1.1 collide directly.
2. **P1 covers commands whose rows belong to P3/P4.** P1 scope is "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" (S:159). The per-row Phase column puts roadmap, save, validate-roadmap and validate-tests in P3, and implement, post-release and pr-submit in P4 (S:109, S:113-114, S:118-119, S:124-125). S:154 and S:225 say P4 waits for D2-D4. AC-1.1 is a P1 gate that must pass before P2 starts (S:154), so it forces edits to the P4 commands before those decisions.
3. **pr-submit.** D3 recommendation (a) is "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (S:240), and S:139 says pr-submit stays a worker candidate "only if the user accepts D3". AC-1.1 requires pr-submit to carry a section in P1. Section 4's "no `--unattended` mode" rule (S:128) is the only command group AC-1.1 excludes, and pr-submit is not in it.

Proof the stated text conflicts: AC-1.1 at S:195, S:76, S:112, S:159, S:240.

Wrong outcome: the P1 gate either never goes green, or a contract-naming section is added to load and to commands whose behavior is undecided.

Required repair (narrowest): restate AC-1.1 and the P1 scope sentence as "every command whose Phase column is P1, plus the six ready commands assigned to P1 in S:159, except load", and state what load gets (nothing, or the flag only). Delete rather than add.

findings.heading: ### F-02 (blocking, MAJOR, Wiegers, priority High)
findings.body:
- **Sentence.** An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a `/sc:load` that changes only its usage line and writes no contract (SPEC:76, SPEC:112, SPEC:265), and builds the P1 acceptance tests that demand a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` for it (SPEC:76 "Every changed command also gains the section", SPEC:195 AC-1.1), so the tests fail on a correct `/sc:load`.
- **Evidence.**
  - SPEC:76: "load has no contract, because it is not dispatched as its own Task"; the same paragraph says "Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section".
  - SPEC:112: load row: Report "none (see note)"; Phase "P1 (usage line only)"; "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task".
  - SPEC:159: load is in the P1 command list; SPEC:79 says the 3.1 table gains the flag, and SPEC:159 says every command in 3.1 and 3.2 accepts it.
  - SPEC:196: AC-1.2 runs the 7.2 live check "on each P1 command" with `--unattended --output <dir>`; 7.2 step 4 (SPEC:183) is `test -s <contract>`, which cannot pass for load.
  - SPEC:265 (Decisions): "a report file would be an unrequested addition."
  - INV-B:31 and INV-B:65 support the load verdict (writes no file; use as a brief step).
- **Wrong outcome.** AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 fail on the `/sc:load` the spec itself specifies; two stated texts contradict each other.
- **Recommendation.** State once that `/sc:load` is exempt from the `## Unattended mode` section, the flag and AC-1.1/AC-1.2 (same treatment as section 4 commands), or remove load from the P1 acceptance scope. Delete or narrow only.
- **Quality impact.** Consistency 6 to 9 for section 3.2 versus section 7.

findings.heading: ### B-1 CRITICAL, blocking: the P1 scope for `--unattended` contradicts itself, AC-1.1 and section 2.3
findings.body:
- **Experts**: Wiegers (lead, consistency and traceability), Adzic (the example below), Whittaker (Sequence Attack).
- **Grading check.** An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, in Phase 1, `--unattended` acceptance and a WC-4 contract "in unattended mode" for every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (SPEC:159), including brainstorm, init-lite and `load`; AC-1.1 then asserts that brainstorm, init-lite and `load` have no `## Unattended mode` section (SPEC:195), so the P1 acceptance check cannot pass. X is wrong because two stated texts contradict each other. The same text builds a second wrong outcome: SPEC:73 tells the coordinator to put `--unattended` in every brief "from Phase P1 on", SPEC:159 makes the flag accepted by every command including those whose gates are converted only in P2 (SPEC:160), and WC-9 (SPEC:67) makes outward defaults off only under the converted command. After P1 and before P2, `/sc:auggie-review <PR> --unattended` is accepted and still posts a review to GitHub by default with no prompt (`cmd/auggie-review.md:51-54` as quoted at SPEC:67 and INV-A:38). That is a safety-boundary outcome, and it needs no guess about the implementer.
- **Evidence**: SPEC:51 (the mode is "the only command-side change"), SPEC:73, SPEC:76 ("Every changed command also gains the section"), SPEC:79 ("the worker reports the named file until Phase 1 adds the contract"), SPEC:84 and SPEC:87 (brainstorm and init-lite: small fix "None"), SPEC:159, SPEC:160, SPEC:195, SPEC:112 (`load` exempt, SPEC:62 exception [F-3]). The line SPEC:79 is also wrong for 6 of the 10 ready commands: only adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo and workflow get a P1 change (SPEC:83,85,86,92).
- **Example (Adzic)**. Given P1 is merged and a coordinator follows SPEC:73, when it dispatches `/sc:brainstorm ... --unattended --output d/`, then the brainstorm command has no flag handling and no section (SPEC:84, SPEC:195); and when it dispatches `/sc:auggie-review 123 --unattended`, then the review is posted (before: 0 reviews, after: 1), against WC-9.
- **Recommendation**: narrow, do not add. State one rule in one place: the flag and the section exist exactly on the commands whose row names the phase being delivered (the 13 of the P1 row, 12 asserted plus `load` as usage-line only); say that SPEC:73 applies to a command only after its phase has passed its checks; say in SPEC:79 that the contract appears for the ready commands in the phase their row names, and that brainstorm and init-lite keep their current report file with no `--unattended` handling and are briefed without it. Delete "(a no-op where a command has no gate)" and "every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" from SPEC:159.
- **Priority**: High. **Quality-impact estimate**: Consistency +2 of 10, Testability +1.

findings.heading: ### B-01 (blocking) AC-1.1 and the P1 scope sentence ask for 37 sections in P1; the same document defers 25 of those commands
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (traceability), Adzic. Priority: High. Label: CRITICAL (dimensional mismatch, FR-19).
- Location: S:159 (P1 scope), S:205 (AC-1.1), against S:250 (D3 a), S:112 and S:275 (load), S:160-162 (P2-P4 scope), S:60 (WC-2).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a Phase 1 that adds a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` to all 37 commands of sections 3.1-3.2 and a passing `test_worker_contract.py` that asserts it, and that is wrong because (a) it includes `pr-submit`, which D3(a) says gets "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (S:250) and which the section 3.2 row still lists as changed (S:114); (b) it includes `load`, whose own row says "Report: none" and whose Decisions entry says a report file "would be an unrequested addition" (S:112, S:275); (c) it includes `implement`, `post-release`, `roadmap`, `cli-eval` and the other P2-P4 commands, so their sections describe gate resolutions that WC-2 says the command performs ("never calls `AskUserQuestion`") while the gate conversion is scheduled for a later phase (S:160-162), and a coordinator that reads those sections after P1 dispatches a worker that still stalls on the prompt; and (d) the test cannot pass for pr-submit under D3(a) without making the change D3(a) rules out.
- Recommendation (narrow, do not add): limit the S:159 flag sentence and AC-1.1 to the commands named in the P1 row of S:159 (12), and let AC-2.1, a P3 check and a P4 check assert the sections for their own commands; state that `load` and the three untouched ready commands get no section, or name the phase that gives it.
- Quality impact: Testability and Consistency.

findings.heading: ### B-02 (CRITICAL, blocking, priority High) P1 acceptance scope contradicts the per-command rows
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers, with Cockburn.
- Location: AC-1.1 and AC-1.2, SPEC:195-196; P1 row, SPEC:159; 3.1 intro, SPEC:79; 3.2 header, SPEC:76; `/sc:load` row, SPEC:112; Decisions, SPEC:265; `/sc:pr-submit` row, SPEC:114; D3, SPEC:238-242; phase intro, SPEC:154.
- Issue (three conflicts):
  1. AC-1.1 asserts that "every command in sections 3.1-3.2" has a section "naming `return-contract.yaml`". `/sc:load` is in 3.2 with "Report: none" and the Decision at SPEC:265 rejects a report file for it. `/sc:load` is also in the P1 list (SPEC:159), so AC-1.2 ("7.2 live check on each P1 command") requires a contract that step 4 (SPEC:183) tests for and the command never writes.
  2. P1 requires "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" (SPEC:159), which includes the P4 commands `/sc:implement`, `/sc:post-release`, `/sc:pr-submit`. D3's recommended option (a) is "no pr-submit changes" (SPEC:240) and SPEC:154 says only P4 waits on D2-D4. A P1 section for pr-submit would define gate resolutions (SPEC:114) that the spec schedules for P4 after a user decision.
  3. 3.1 says the ready commands' "only command changes are the small fixes in the last column" (SPEC:79), and `brainstorm` and `init-lite` have "None" there and appear in no phase row (SPEC:159-162), yet AC-1.1 requires both to carry the new section and a `--unattended` flag. In P1 the flag is "a no-op where a command has no gate" (SPEC:159), which does not say what the flag does on a gated command (auggie-review posts, cleanup prompts) until P2, although SPEC:73 tells coordinators to pass `--unattended` "from Phase 1 on".
- Recommendation: restrict AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 to the commands whose phase row is P1 (plus the 3.1 commands the spec chooses to touch), exclude `load` from the contract assertion, and state in one line which phase adds the flag to each gated command.
- Quality impact: removes a P1 gate that cannot be passed and a hidden decision on D3.

findings.heading: ### B-2 (blocking) AC-1.1 requires a section that the `load` and `brainstorm` rows say will not exist
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (traceability), Cockburn (who is served), Adzic (the test is the example).
- Stated texts that contradict each other:
  1. AC-1.1 (SPEC:201): the test asserts that EVERY command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`.
  2. WC-4 (SPEC:62) exempts `load` ("writes no file"); its row (SPEC:112) says report "none", change "P1 (usage line only)"; P1 scope (SPEC:159) both lists `load` as "usage line only" and says the flag is accepted by every command in 3.1 and 3.2.
  3. The `brainstorm` row (SPEC:84) lists "Small fix: None" and a contract that already exists, while SPEC:76 says every changed command gains the section and AC-1.1 requires it for every 3.1 command.
- An implementer who follows the load row builds a usage-line fix only, and the spec's own test AC-1.1 then fails on `load`, so P1 cannot pass; an implementer who follows AC-1.1 adds to `load` a section naming `return-contract.yaml`, a file the same spec says `load` must not write. The spec does not say which text wins.
- Recommendation: make AC-1.1 enumerate its set ("every command in 3.1-3.2 except `load`", or require `load` only to name the exemption), and change the `brainstorm` "None" to "section only".
- Priority: High. Quality impact: P1 acceptance is unsatisfiable as written.

findings.heading: ### F2. MAJOR, blocking. P1 scope and AC-1.1 require unattended support in commands whose behavior P2 to P4 and D2 to D4 decide
findings.body:
- **Expert:** Fowler (phase boundaries follow dependencies), Wiegers.
- **Location:** section 6 P1 row (line 159) and intro (line 154), AC-1.1 (line 195), P4 row (line 162), section 9 intro (line 225), D3 (lines 238-242), section 4 last paragraph (line 139), 3.2 rows `pr-submit`, `post-release`, `implement`, `auggie-review` (lines 100, 109, 113, 114).
- **Issue:** P1 is "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)". AC-1.1 requires a `## Unattended mode` section in every command of 3.1 and 3.2 except `load`. That includes `pr-submit`, `post-release` and `implement` (P4) and the gate commands of P2. Section 6 says P4 "waits for answers to D2-D4", and section 9 says phases 0 to 3 proceed on the recommendations. The recommendation for D3 is (a), "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4", and line 139 says `pr-submit` is a worker candidate "only if the user accepts D3".
- **Grading check:** An implementer who follows P1 and AC-1.1 as written adds `--unattended` and a contract-naming `## Unattended mode` section to `/sc:pr-submit`, `/sc:post-release` and `/sc:implement`, and that is wrong because (1) under the recommended D3 (a) `pr-submit` must not become a worker command at all, so AC-1.1 cannot pass without contradicting D3 (a); (2) section 6 says each phase is "independently useful", yet after P1 a brief containing `--unattended` reaches `post-release` and `auggie-review` still prompting and still taking their outward defaults, which violates WC-2 and WC-9 ("under `--unattended` ... any default that pushes, opens a PR, posts ... is off") until P2 or P4 ships. The parenthetical "no-op where a command has no gate" leaves the gated commands undefined at P1.
- **Recommendation:** limit P1 (flag, section, AC-1.1) to the commands P1 lists in its Commands column; add each remaining command in the phase that delivers its gate resolution; make the pr-submit row of AC-1.1 conditional on D3 (b). Prefer deleting the "every command in 3.1 and 3.2" wording over adding a new rule.
- **Priority:** High. **Quality impact:** consistency +1.5, completeness +0.5.

=== ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS ===

No architecture finding reaches blocking. Medium and minor architecture findings are M1, M3, M5, M9, M12, M13 and n3, n9 below. The core decision (sections 1.1 to 1.3) holds against CAPS:97-103, 147-150, 155 and INV-A:13-14.

findings.heading: ### B-1 (blocking) AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 test 12 P1 commands; section 6 and the section 3 rows give the flag, the section and the contract to 8 or 9
findings.body:
- Severity: CRITICAL by FR-19 (dimensional mismatch with concrete counts), blocking on consequence. Experts: Wiegers, Fowler, Whittaker (Divergence Attack).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text builds either (a) `## Unattended mode` sections naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` on all 12 commands whose section 3 phase is P1, or (b) the 8 or 9 commands section 6 lists. (a) is wrong because the load row says its report is "none (see note)" and that it is "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task" (SPEC:112), and the three ready P1 rows (adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo) specify only a filename or location fix, with no unattended gates and no contract (SPEC:83, 85, 86); section 6 says those three are "fixes", not flag recipients (SPEC:159). (b) is wrong because AC-1.1 is a test the same spec requires and it asserts the section on "every command whose section 3 phase is P1" (SPEC:195), so it fails on the commands not given one. Two stated texts contradict each other.
- Concrete count trace:
  - Section 3 rows with phase P1: ready rows adversarial (SPEC:83), cleanup-audit (SPEC:85), index-repo (SPEC:86) = 3; change rows analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, load, test (SPEC:99, 101, 102, 106, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123) = 9. N = 12.
  - Section 6 P1 flag/section recipients: analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test = 8, plus load "(usage line only)" = 9 at most (SPEC:159).
  - AC-1.1 consumes N = 12 (SPEC:195). AC-1.2 runs "each P1 command with `--unattended --output <dir>`" (SPEC:196); index-repo and cleanup-audit have no `--output` flag and no `--unattended` flag in their rows (INV-A:42, 53), and load takes neither.
- Recommendation (Reviser brief carries it): narrow AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 to the commands section 6 lists as flag recipients, name them, and state that load, adversarial, cleanup-audit and index-repo are tested only by their named fix (AC-1.4 already covers adversarial, SPEC:198). Do not add a section to load, adversarial, cleanup-audit or index-repo.
- Priority: High. Quality-impact estimate: +1 testability, +1 consistency.

findings.heading: **F2. CRITICAL (blocking). Expert: Adzic (concrete examples), Wiegers, Whittaker (Divergence Attack). Two acceptance checks and the `load` row contradict each other.**
findings.body:
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written gives `/sc:load` "usage line only" and no report file (`spec:112`, `spec:159`, Decision at `spec:265`: "a report file would be an unrequested addition. Only its usage-line defect is fixed"), and `load` is also named as a P1 command (`spec:159`). AC-1.1 asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` (`spec:195`), and AC-1.2 runs the 7.2 live check on each P1 command (`spec:196`), whose step 4 needs a contract file (`spec:183`). `load` is in section 3.2 (`spec:112`). So AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 cannot pass for `load` without breaking the stated Decision, and P1 cannot be declared passed.
- I can break this specification by **Divergence Attack**. The invariant at **spec:195** ("every command in sections 3.1-3.2") fails when **one command in the quantified set is explicitly exempt from the property (spec:112, spec:265)**. Concrete attack: the test iterates the 37 commands (Quantity Flow Diagram); 36 have the section, `load.md` has none (usage-line fix only); `uv run pytest tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py` fails; adding the section to make it pass makes `load` name a contract it never writes, or adds the "unrequested" report file the Decision rejects.
- Recommendation: either move `load` out of the AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 sets in one clause ("except `load`, usage-line fix only"), or move it to the list of commands that are not dispatched. Do not add a report file.
- Priority: High.

findings.heading: ### F1. MAJOR, blocking. AC-1.1 and AC-1.2 require a report and an `## Unattended mode` section for `/sc:load`, while the spec says `/sc:load` gets neither
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers.
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written changes only the Usage line of `/sc:load` in Phase 1 and writes no report for it (SPEC:112, SPEC:159, SPEC:265), and then AC-1.1 (SPEC:195) demands a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` for every command in sections 3.1-3.2, and AC-1.2 (SPEC:196) demands a live run with `--unattended --output <dir>` whose pass step 4 needs a valid contract (SPEC:183) for "each P1 command", which includes load (SPEC:159). Load has no report, no output flag and "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task" (SPEC:112), so Phase 1 cannot pass; because later phases wait for earlier checks (SPEC:154), Phases 2-4 are blocked.
- Evidence: SPEC:76 ("Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section"); SPEC:112 (Report: "none (see note)"); SPEC:265 (decision: "a report file would be an unrequested addition"); SPEC:159 (load listed in P1); SPEC:195-196; INV-B:31, INV-B:62, INV-B:65 (load writes no file and is better used as a brief step). Also SPEC:220 (non-goal 8: only defects that stop a command working as a worker are in scope) and SPEC:112 (the only change is a Usage-line defect that does not stop it working as a worker).
- Recommendation: delete load from the P1 command list (SPEC:159), from AC-1.1/AC-1.2 and from the "27 needing a change" count, or state in AC-1.1/AC-1.2 that load is exempt. Narrowing is smaller than adding a report to load.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Testability 6 to 8.

findings.heading: ### REQ-2 (blocking, MAJOR, Wiegers with Cockburn): the P1 acceptance test contradicts the rows' own phase assignments and the "ready today" rows
findings.body:
Where: `spec:79`, `spec:87` and `spec:84` (3.1 "Small fix: None"), `spec:112` (load), `spec:76` and `spec:95`, `spec:159` (P1 scope), `spec:195` (AC-1.1), `spec:154`.

Text as written:
- P1 delivers "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" and AC-1.1 requires every command in 3.1-3.2 to have a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` (`spec:159`, `spec:195`).
- But 3.1 says for the ready commands "The only command changes are the small fixes in the last column" (`spec:79`), and brainstorm and init-lite have "Small fix: None" (`spec:84`, `spec:87`).
- load's row says "Report: none (see note)", "Other required change: none: use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task", Phase "P1 (usage line only)" (`spec:112`), and the Decisions table says a report file for load "would be an unrequested addition" (`spec:265`). Yet `spec:76` says "Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section", and load is changed.
- The rows assign implement, post-release and pr-submit to P4, roadmap, save and validate-* to P3, and the gate commands to P2 (`spec:109`, `spec:113`, `spec:114`, `spec:118-119`, `spec:124-125`); yet AC-1.1 is a P1 check over all of 3.1-3.2.

Grading check: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, for P1, a test that fails until brainstorm, init-lite, load, implement, post-release, pr-submit, roadmap, save, validate-roadmap and validate-tests each carry a `## Unattended mode` section naming a contract file (or builds the P1 plan and leaves the test red), and that is wrong because the rows say brainstorm, init-lite and load are not to be changed beyond a usage line and the later-phase commands are not to be touched before their phase; the P1 pass condition and the per-row scope cannot both hold.

Secondary consequence (the same text): a P1 `## Unattended mode` section and an accepted `--unattended` on a gate command such as auggie-review, which does not turn off PR posting or the remediation offer until P2 (`spec:100`, `spec:160`), gives a coordinator a switch that looks safe and is not. The spec never says `--unattended` must not be used on a command before its own phase. I grade that part Medium (M-4) because it also needs the assumption that P1 is released and used before P2.

Recommendation: scope AC-1.1 to the commands whose row says P1 (and the 3.1 commands the P1 row names), or delete the clause "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" from `spec:159`; give load and the "None" rows an explicit exemption.

findings.heading: ### B2. CRITICAL (blocking). Phase 1 and its acceptance check demand work that other parts of the spec say must not happen
findings.body:
- Experts: Wiegers (consistency), Cockburn (who acts when), Fowler (phase boundaries).
- Quoted texts:
  - `spec:195`, AC-1.1: the test "asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`".
  - `spec:159`, P1 scope: "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2".
  - Against it, `spec:112`, load row: report "none (see note)"; "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task". And `spec:265`: "a report file would be an unrequested addition."
  - Against it, `spec:240`, D3 recommended option (a): "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4", with `spec:154`: "Phases 1-3 need no user decision; Phase 4 waits for answers to D2-D4", and `spec:162` placing implement, post-release and pr-submit in P4.
  - Against it, `spec:159` itself lists only 13 commands in the P1 Commands column, while reflect, release-split, tdd, troubleshoot are scheduled in P2 (`spec:160`) and brainstorm, init-lite in no phase (see the Quantity Flow above).
- Wrong outcome: An implementer who follows AC-1.1 as written must give `load` an Unattended-mode section naming `return-contract.yaml`, which the load row and decision at `spec:265` say must not exist; and must edit pr-submit, implement and post-release in Phase 1 before the user answers D2 to D4, which `spec:154` and `spec:240` forbid. An implementer who follows the load row and the D3 recommendation builds a Phase 1 that fails its own acceptance check, so the phase gate in `spec:154` ("Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks in section 7 pass") blocks every later phase. The two texts cannot both hold.
- Recommendation: restrict AC-1.1 and the P1 flag sentence to the commands the P1 row lists, exempt load, and state which phase adds the section for each remaining command; delete the sentence that gives P4 commands a P1 section, or make it conditional on the D2 to D4 answers.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: the rollout cannot be completed in the stated order.

findings.heading: ### F1 - CRITICAL-by-consequence, BLOCKING: AC-1.1 and the P1 sweep contradict the `/sc:load` row and its recorded Decision
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (traceability), Adzic (acceptance example).
- Stated texts that contradict:
  - Spec line 195 (AC-1.1): the test "asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`".
  - Spec line 159 (P1): the `--unattended` flag is "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2", and line 76: "Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section"; WC-4 (line 62): in unattended mode the command "writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`" on every outcome.
  - Spec line 112 (`load` row, section 3.2): Report column "none (see note)", Resume "n/a", "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task", Phase "P1 (usage line only)". Spec line 265 (Decisions): "Use it inside a brief ... a report file would be an unrequested addition. Only its usage-line defect is fixed." `INV-B:65` supports that: "it only loads context into the current session and writes no file".
- Wrong outcome (grading sentence): An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds either an AC-1.1 test that fails on `load` (it has no `## Unattended mode` section and no contract by the row and the Decision), or a `load` that gains a section and a contract file that the row and Decision say must not exist; both cannot hold, so the P1 gate "every check in its block passes" (spec line 167) cannot be met by following the spec, and the phase can never be declared passed without picking which of the two texts to break.
- Same contradiction, smaller scope: `/sc:init-lite` is in section 3.1 with "Small fix: None" (line 87) yet is inside the P1 sweep of "every command in 3.1" (line 159) and AC-1.1/AC-1.2. Noted under this id, not a separate finding.
- Recommendation: narrow AC-1.1 and the P1 sentence to "every command in 3.1-3.2 except `load`" (or say `load` gets a section that states it writes no contract). Prefer narrowing over adding.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: acceptance gate for P1 is unsatisfiable as written.

findings.heading: ### B2. CRITICAL (blocking). AC-1.1 cannot pass for `/sc:load`, because P1 gives load only a usage-line fix and load writes no contract
findings.body:
- Experts: Wiegers (traceability from requirement to check), Crispin-style completeness check by Adzic.
- Stated texts:
  - `spec:195` (AC-1.1): "the test asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`".
  - `spec:112` (3.2 load): Report "none (see note)", Resume "n/a", Other change "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task; separately, `--checkpoint` is missing from its Usage line". Phase "P1 (usage line only)".
  - `spec:159` (P1): load is listed as "(usage line only)", while the same row says the `--unattended` flag is "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2".
  - `spec:265` (Decisions): "a report file would be an unrequested addition. Only its usage-line defect is fixed."
  - `spec:76`: "Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section".
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows P1 and the Decisions row builds `/sc:load` with only a usage-line fix and no `## Unattended mode` section, because load writes no contract. That is wrong because `test_worker_contract.py` (AC-1.1) requires every 3.1-3.2 command, load included, to carry a section naming `return-contract.yaml`, so the P1 pass condition (`spec:168`, "a phase passes only when every check ... passes") cannot be met. The other reading, adding a section that names a contract load never writes, contradicts WC-4 and the Decisions row.
- Recommendation: narrow AC-1.1 to "every command in 3.1-3.2 except `load`", or move load out of the AC-1.1 set and state that load takes no `--unattended` section. One line in AC-1.1 and one in P1 is enough.

findings.heading: **B2 (MAJOR, blocking). AC-1.1 requires every command in sections 3.1-3.2 to name `return-contract.yaml`, but the `/sc:load` row and the Decisions table say `/sc:load` has no report file.**
findings.body:
- Stated texts that contradict:
  - spec:195 (AC-1.1): the test asserts "every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`".
  - spec:112 (`load` row): report "none (see note)", resume "n/a", change is "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task", usage-line fix in P1.
  - spec:265 (Decisions): "Use it inside a brief ... a report file would be an unrequested addition."
  - spec:53 (section 2.1): each section "lists only its own gate resolutions and report file".
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the `load` row and the Decisions row builds a `/sc:load` section with no report file and no `return-contract.yaml`, and that is wrong because AC-1.1, the P1 gate (spec:154, "Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks pass"), cannot pass; the only way to pass is to add a report file to `/sc:load`, which spec:265 rejects.
- Expert attribution: Wiegers (traceability and testability), Crispin (acceptance criterion cannot pass).
- Recommendation: narrow AC-1.1 to the commands that write a contract (exclude `load`), or state what `load`'s section says in place of the contract name.
- Priority: High.

findings.heading: ### B1: the P1 acceptance test requires an `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` in `/sc:load`, which the same spec says gets no contract
findings.body:
- Severity: MAJOR, graded blocking (two stated texts contradict). Expert: Wiegers, Adzic. Priority: High.
- Texts:
  - `spec:195`: AC-1.1 "the test asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`".
  - `spec:112`: the `load` row in 3.2: Report "none (see note)", Resume "n/a", "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task"; `spec:159` lists "load (usage line only)" as the P1 scope.
  - `spec:265` (Decisions): for `/sc:load`, "a report file would be an unrequested addition. Only its usage-line defect is fixed." Supported by INV-B:31 and INV-B:65 ("writes no file").
  - `spec:76`: "Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section", and load's only change is the usage line.
- Wrong outcome: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds P1 so that `/sc:load` gets only the usage-line fix (spec:112, 159, 265), and X is wrong because AC-1.1 (spec:195) then fails for `load`, so the P1 gate cannot pass; the only way to pass is to add an unattended section and a contract to `load`, which spec:265 rejects. The same assertion also covers the 3.1 commands whose "small fix" is "None" (brainstorm, init-lite, spec:84, 87) although spec:79 says their only change is that fix; and, as written, the commands that P2-P4 edit (spec:160-162), which P1 does not touch.
- Concrete attack (Whittaker, Sequence): run the P1 gate (spec:154 "Later phases do not start until the earlier phase's checks pass") with the spec's own scope: test goes red on `load` and on every P2-P4 command, P2 never starts.

findings.heading: ### B4 (MAJOR, blocking, Wiegers / Adzic): AC-1.1 requires a contract-naming section in `/sc:load`, which section 3 and the Decisions table say has no report
findings.body:
Quoted texts:
- S:195 (AC-1.1): every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section "naming `return-contract.yaml`".
- S:112 (load): Report "none (see note)"; "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task".
- S:265 (Decisions): "a report file would be an unrequested addition. Only its usage-line defect is fixed."
- S:159 (P1): load is "usage line only".

An implementer who follows the stated text as written either adds a contract to `/sc:load` (contradicting S:112 and S:265, and SA-3 at S:148) or leaves it out and fails AC-1.1. The criterion cannot pass with the other stated texts both honoured. Section 3.2 also counts `/sc:load` among "27 needing a change" (S:76) although its only change is a usage-line fix, so the 10 / 27 / 6 split in S:76 and S:128 does not describe the work the P1 test asserts.

findings.heading: ### F1 - BLOCKING - `/sc:load` cannot satisfy both AC-1.1 and its own row
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (traceability), Adzic (acceptance), Crispin (testability). Severity label: MAJOR, graded blocking by consequence. Priority High.
- Stated texts that contradict:
  - AC-1.1: the test "asserts that every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`" (SPEC:195). `load` is a section 3.2 row (SPEC:112).
  - Section 3 intro: "Every changed command also gains the `## Unattended mode` section" (SPEC:76); `load` is changed (usage line, SPEC:112). P1 scope: the `--unattended` flag is "accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" (SPEC:159).
  - The `load` row: Report (WC-4) = "none (see note)", "use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task" (SPEC:112). The Decisions table: "a report file would be an unrequested addition. Only its usage-line defect is fixed" (SPEC:265). WC-4 itself says an unattended command "writes `<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml`" on every outcome (SPEC:62).
- Sentence: an implementer who follows AC-1.1 adds a `## Unattended mode` section to `load` that names `return-contract.yaml`, which creates the report file SPEC:265 forbids; an implementer who follows SPEC:112 and SPEC:265 leaves `load` without it, and AC-1.1 (a P1 gate, SPEC:154) cannot pass. Either way one stated text is violated, with no guess needed.
- Basis in the inventory: `load` writes no file and its only output is context in chat (INV-B:31, INV-B:65), so SPEC:112/265 are the better-supported side; AC-1.1 and SPEC:159 are what must narrow.
- Recommendation: exclude `load` by name from AC-1.1 and from the P1 flag scope (or state in the row that it gets a section that says "no report file; not dispatched as its own Task"). Narrow, do not add.
